text:
Jess: Hey, seeing large latency spikes after today's SDK update. Our app usually hits < 40ms but now a lot of requests go to EU and spike to ~220ms. We set x-redwood-region: us-west in our client headers — why is it routing to eu-west?
Anna (support): Sorry — can you paste the exact raw header value you send (no redaction)? a curl example is fine.
Jess: sure. here's what we sent (copy-pasted from our client):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" \
  -H "x-redwood-region: ｕｓ－ｗｅｓｔ" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Jess: note the region there looks normal in our editor, but it's not ascii — we pasted from internal config.
Anna (support): ah interesting. forwarding to oncall to confirm.
Raj (oncall): looking at the ingress logs for that request id 6f3a... I can see the raw header bytes logged as: `x-redwood-region=\uFF55\uFF53\uFF0D\uFF57\uFF45\uFF53\uFF54` (fullwidth chars). Router compares normalized ascii tokens so it doesn't match `us-west` and falls back to our geo-based nearest POP -> eu-west.
Mike (router): yep — router only does case-fold + trim, we weren't running Unicode NFK normalization. Fullwidth letters/dash are different codepoints (U+FF55 etc.) so the token table miss. Proposed: apply NFKC normalization on region header on ingress and add a new metric/rate-limited log when header normalization changes value so we can catch messy clients. Quick patch: normalize -> check mapping -> route; fallback unchanged.
Anna (support): can we repro locally so we can give customer mitigation steps?
Raj (oncall): repro steps:
1) `printf "\xEF\xBC\xB5\xEF\xBC\x53\xEF\xBC\x8D\xEF\xBC\x57\xEF\xBC\x45\xEF\xBC\x53\xEF\xBC\x54"` will create fullwidth `ｕｓ－ｗｅｓｔ`.
2) `curl -H "x-redwood-region: $(printf ...)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/gen`
Observed router log: `region_header_raw=\uFF55\uFF53\uFF0D\uFF57... region_resolved=fallback-pop=eu-west`
Mike (router): patch ready: normalize at ingress (NFKC) + add metric `region_header_normalized` with tag (original,val_after) and rate-limit log. I'll canary this to 10% on prod edge config.
SRE-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for router-ingress-normalize v2 -> 10% edges.
Jess: the customer is also asking about billing — these routed EU requests triggered cross-region egress and they saw a cost spike yesterday. Can we give a credit?
Anna (support): I've opened a billing ticket and flagged as P1 for suspected misrouting due to header encoding. Will ask billing to evaluate credits while we fix.
Mike (router): temporary mitigation for customers: set the query param `?region=us-west` or send header using plain ascii hyphen-minus (- U+002D) until canary completes. We'll post a short KB note.
Raj (oncall): monitoring alert added: count of normalized headers >0 in last 1h. We'll watch for any other odd unicode variants.
Anna (support): customer notified with repro, workaround, and ETA: patch canary 10% now, full roll 15m if no regressions.
Jess: customer confirmed applying the ASCII header fixed latency immediately. thanks.
Mike (router): canary looks good, promoting to 100% in 12m. :shipit:
SRE-bot: deploy-bot: rollout complete -> router-ingress-normalize v2 -> 100%
Anna (support): closing loop with customer and billing. Follow-up: we should add a short content note in SDK docs advising ASCII region tokens and perhaps client-side normalization helper.
Jess: appreciated, will relay to engineering.
